## Building (rounds 217, 618)

Everything builds on the pilot's toolchain (`../../lean-toolchain`, Mathlib at `../../MATHLIB_REV`):

```
../../build.sh    # the pilot's own files
./build.sh        # PNT+ and this directory
```

`build.sh` does four things:
- It takes the 19 PNT+ files that this directory imports, at commit `650d312` (Lean v4.33.1), into `upstream/`. Set `PNT` to a PNT+ clone to use it; otherwise that one commit is fetched.
- It applies `pnt_port.patch`, which ports those files to the pilot's toolchain. There are five small changes, all forced by Mathlib API drift; the top of the patch lists them.
- It compiles `Architect.lean`, the PNT+ files and this directory's files into `../../build`, next to the pilot's oleans. Since round 618 a module is compiled only if its olean is missing or older than its source or than the olean of a module it imports (one of the pilot's, PNT+'s or this directory's; Mathlib's oleans are not compared), one module at a time, so after an edit only that file and its dependents are rebuilt; `FORCE=1` compiles every module. The script prints `== M` before compiling `M` and `-- M: Ns` after, then the counts compiled and up to date.
  - `Architect.lean` is a no-op stand-in for LeanArchitect, the package behind PNT+'s `@[blueprint]` tags. The tags only feed PNT+'s blueprint document.
  - The PNT+ files are compiled with PNT+'s own lakefile options, `autoImplicit = false` and `relaxedAutoImplicit = false`.
- It prints the axioms of the final theorems, on every run. It fails if Lean reports a use of `sorry` in one of this directory's files that it compiles, or if such a file or the final check prints an axiom outside `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The final check also needs one clean line per `#print axioms` (round 327).

The pilot's layer I–II files (`Vinogradov` … `VinoKV`) are no longer copied and renamed: `KVBridge.lean` and `LandauKV.lean` import the pilot's own oleans. `kv_port.sh` is gone.

The two `sorry` lemmas in PNT+'s `Wiener.lean` are not in the dependency cone of any theorem here. So the build does not check the PNT+ files (`StrongPNT.lean`, which prints its axioms under `open Classical` as `[propext, choice, Quot.sound]`, would also fail the check). A checked theorem here that used one of the two lemmas would print `sorryAx` in its axiom line and fail the build.

## WanderLadderPNT.lean (round 191)

`WanderLadderPNT.lean` restates two PNT+ results in the pilot's terms (`Chebyshev.psi` from Mathlib):
- rung 1, the prime number theorem;
- rung 2, de la Vallée Poussin's error term.

All three theorems print only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

## Rung3.lean (round 192)

`rung3_of_region` reduces rung 3 to one analytic input, `KVInput n₁ n₂`: a zero-free region of width `(log t)^{−n₁}` plus a log-derivative bound. Its axioms are clean.

## Landau.lean (round 193)

This is layer III of rung 3, Landau's lemma in general form. Three of its proofs raise `maxHeartbeats`. *(Round 509: two; `near_boundW` compiles without its override, which is removed.)*

`rung3_of_growth` runs from `PolylogGrowth a K` (`|ζ| ≤ K(log|t|)^K` on `σ ≥ 1 − (log|t|)^{−a}`, `0 < a ≤ 1`) to `ψ(x) − x = O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/(1+n₁)}))`, for every `n₁ > a`. The intermediate outputs are `zeroFree_of_growth` (the zero-free region) and `logDerivBnd_of_growth` (`|ζ'/ζ| ≤ C(log|t|)³`). All axioms are clean.

The local steps are proved once, for any admissible width `w` (`WidthOK`: positive, at most 1, non-increasing, `log(1/w(L)) = O(1 + log L)`): `apply_localW`, `zero_gapW`, `disc_factsW`, `near_boundW`. The power width `wpow a L = L^(−a)` gives the statements above, and `LandauKV`/`LogDerivKV` use the Korobov–Vinogradov width. Round 215's `LandauW.lean` is merged in (round 219).

## KVBridge.lean (round 212): rung 3, unconditional

- `zeroFree_kv`: `ZetaZeroFreeGenProp n₁` holds for every `n₁ > 2/3`, i.e. ζ has no zeros in `σ ≥ 1 − A/(log|t|)^{n₁}`.
- `rung3_kv`: `ψ(x) − x = O(x·exp(−c(log x)^{1/(1+n₁)}))` for every `n₁ > 2/3`.

## Rounds 215–216: the Korobov–Vinogradov prime number theorem

- `LandauKV.zeroFree_KV`: ζ has no zeros in `σ ≥ 1 − A/((log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3})`, for `|t| ≥ e³`.
- `LogDerivKV.logDerivBnd_KV`: `|ζ'/ζ| ≤ C(log|t|)³` for `|t| > 3` and `σ ≥ 1 − A·u(|t|)`, where `u(T) = 1/((log T)^{2/3}(log(log T + 3))^{1/3})`.

## SmoothPerron.lean (rounds 472, 473, 484)

`SmoothPerron.verticalIntegral_eq_smoothedSum` is PNT+'s `SmoothedChebyshevDirichlet` for any `f` with `f(0) = 0` and `L(f, σ)` absolutely convergent, `1 < σ ≤ 2`: `(1/2πi) ∫_{(σ)} L(f, s)𝓜(Smooth1)(s)X^s ds = Σ_n f(n)Smooth1(n/X)`. `verticalIntegral_shift` moves a vertical integral across a strip on which the integrand is complex-differentiable and tends to `0` uniformly as `|Im s| → ∞` (PNT+'s `DiffVertRect_eq_UpperLowerUs` and `HolomorphicOn.vanishesOnRectangle`). `smoothedSum_eq_verticalIntegral_left` combines the two for a function `L` equal to `L(f, s)` on `Re s > 1`, complex-differentiable on `Re s ≥ σ′` with at most linear growth there. `mellin_le_geom` bounds `𝓜(Smooth1)` on `Re s = σ ∈ (0, 1]` by `Kε^{−κ}(1 + |t|)^{−1−κ}`, the geometric mean of round 338's `MediumPNTW.MellinOfSmooth1d` and PNT+'s `MellinOfSmooth1b`, and `norm_smoothedSum_sub_le` bounds the cost of the smoothing by `B(3 log 2 · εX + 1)` when `|f(n)| ≤ B` for `n ≤ 3X`. Round 473 split the shift out of `smoothedSum_eq_verticalIntegral_left` as `verticalIntegral_integrand_shift`: the line moves from `Re s = 2` to `Re s = σ′` for any `L` complex-differentiable on `Re s ≥ σ′`, bounded on `Re s = 2`, with at most linear growth there. `DivisorExponent.lean` applies it to `g_k`, the entire part of `ζ(s)^k`. Round 484 split `mellin_le_geom` as `mellin_le_geom_of`, the same bound from given constants `B/|s|` and `C/(ε|s|²)`, with the constant `B^{1−κ}C^κ(σ/2)^{−1−κ}`; `ExplicitSmooth.lean` applies it with `B = 25` and `C = 54`. *(Round 513: `norm_LSeries_le_of_le_re`, `|L(f, s)| ≤ Σ|f(n)|n^{−σ₀}` on `Re s ≥ σ₀`, moved here from `ChiPNT.lean` and replaces `norm_LSeries_le`, its case `Re s = σ₀`. See the main README, round 513.)*

## MertensExponent.lean (round 472)

`MertensExponent.mertens_isBigO_of_zeroFree`: if `ζ(s) ≠ 0` on `Re s > θ`, `0 ≤ θ < 1`, then `M(x) = Σ_{n≤x} μ(n) = O(x^{θ+η})` for every `η > 0`. The proof moves the smoothed Perron integral of `1/ζ` to `Re s = θ + η₀/4`, with `1/ζ = (s − 1)/Z(s)` through the pilot's entire `PsiOmega.Zr` and the bounds of `HalfPlaneLindelof.zeta_bound_of_zeroFree`. At `θ = 11/12` and at `θ = Θ` it needs no hypothesis. With the pilot's `MertensOmega.mertens_omega`: `limsup log|M(x)| / log x = Θ` (`limsup_mexpo`), `RH ⟺ Θ = ½` (`rh_iff_Theta_eq_half`), `RH ⟺ M(x) = O(x^{½+η})` for every `η > 0` (`rh_iff_mertens`), and the partial sums of `Σ μ(n)n^{−s}` converge for `Re s > Θ` and diverge for `Re s < Θ` (`moebius_tendsto_of_Theta_lt`, `moebius_not_tendsto_of_lt_Theta`), so the abscissa of convergence is `Θ` (`moebiusAbscissa_eq_Theta`). The convergence is Abel summation as in Mathlib's `LSeries_eq_mul_integral`, without its hypothesis of absolute convergence (`tendsto_partialSum_of_isBigO`).

## DivisorExponent.lean (round 473)

`DivisorExponent.divisor_isBigO_of_zeroFree`: if `ζ(s) ≠ 0` on `Re s > θ`, `0 ≤ θ < 1`, then for every `k ≥ 1` and `η > 0`, `Σ_{n≤x} d_k(n) = xP_k(log x) + O(x^{θ+η})`. Here `d_k` is the `k`-th Dirichlet power of `ArithmeticFunction.zeta` (`dk k`), and `P_k` (`Pk k`) is a real polynomial of degree `k − 1` with leading coefficient `1/(k − 1)!` (`natDegree_Pk_eq`, `coeff_Pk`). The proof writes `ζ(s)^k` as its principal part at `1` plus an entire `g_k` (`zeta_pow_eq`, by iterated `dslope` of `Z(s)^k` with the pilot's `PsiOmega.Zr`). It integrates the principal part exactly (`verticalIntegral_inv_sub_one_pow`, through `(s − 1)^{−m} = ∫_0^∞ u^{m−1}e^{−(s−1)u} du/(m − 1)!`, Fubini and Mathlib's Mellin inversion), moves the line for `g_k` to `Re s = θ + η₀/4` with `HalfPlaneLindelof.zeta_bound_of_zeroFree` (`norm_remainder_le`), and unsmooths by comparing two smoothed sums, since `d_k ≥ 0` (`tsum_smooth_le`, `le_tsum_smooth`). At `θ = 11/12` and at `θ = Θ` it needs no hypothesis (`divisor_isBigO_eleven_twelfths`, `divisor_isBigO_Theta`). See the main README, round 473. All axioms are clean.

## Littlewood.lean (rounds 480, 482, 484)

`Littlewood.norm_LSeries_le_of_sum_le` is partial summation for an L-series (Mathlib's `LSeries_eq_mul_integral`): partial sums at most `Kt^α`, `0 ≤ α < σ`, give `|L(f, σ)| ≤ σK/(σ − α)`. `Littlewood.logDeriv_le_loglog` bounds `|L′/L(σ, χ)|` by `M log log(N + 16)` on `1 < σ ≤ 2`, interpolating Chebyshev's `ψ(t) ≤ (log 4 + 4)t` with `ChiUniform.psiChi_le_uniform` at the exponent `1/log log(N + 16)`. The mean value theorem for `log|L(σ, χ)|` on `[1, 1 + 1/log log(N + 16)]` gives `Littlewood.abs_log_norm_LFunction_one_le`, `|log|L(1, χ)|| ≤ log log log(N + 16) + C`, and so `c/log log(N + 16) ≤ |L(1, χ)| ≤ C′ log log(N + 16)` (`norm_LFunction_one_ge`, `norm_LFunction_one_le`), for every quadratic `χ ≠ 1` mod `N`. Round 482 added `Littlewood.norm_logDeriv_one_le`, `|L′/L(1, χ)| ≤ M log log(N + 16)`: the bound of `logDeriv_le_loglog` at `σ = 1`, by continuity, since `L(1, χ) ≠ 0` (round 477). Round 484 added the `_of` forms, each bound from a given constant: `logDeriv_le_loglog_of` (`48(log 4 + 4 + C₁)e` from `|ψ(x, χ)| ≤ C₁ log(N + 2)·x^{23/24}`), `abs_log_norm_LFunction_one_le_of` (`M + log 2`), `norm_LFunction_one_le_of` and `norm_LFunction_one_ge_of` (`e^{±C}`), and `norm_logDeriv_one_le_of`. See the main README, rounds 480, 482 and 484. All axioms are clean.

## LeastNonresidue.lean (rounds 482, 484)

`LeastNonresidue.re_psiChi_ge`: if `χ(p) = ε = ±1` at every prime `p ≤ x` with `p ∤ q`, then `ε·Re ψ(x, χ) ≥ ψ(x) − 4√x log x − log q`, with Mathlib's `Chebyshev.psi_sub_theta_le` for the prime powers and `sum_log_prime_dvd_le`, `Σ_{p∣q} log p ≤ log q`, for the primes dividing `q`. Against round 480's `ChiUniform.psiChi_le_uniform` at `η = 1/12 − 1/A` and `ψ(x) ≥ x/4` for `x ≥ 100` (`psi_ge_quarter`, from Mathlib's `Chebyshev.psi_ge'`), this forces `x^{1/A} ≤ K log(q + 2)` (`rpow_le_of_forall_eq`): Ankeny's argument. So for every `A > 12`, every quadratic `χ ≠ 1` mod `q` has a prime `p ∤ q` with `χ(p) = 1` and one with `χ(p) = −1` below `C(log(q + 2))^A` (`exists_prime_eq`). With the Legendre character (`legendreChar`, Mathlib's `quadraticChar (ZMod p)`), every odd prime `p` has a quadratic nonresidue `n ≤ C(log p)^A` (`exists_nonsquare_le`), and `n ≤ C_δ p^δ` for every `δ > 0` (`exists_nonsquare_le_rpow`). Round 484 added the `_of` forms: `rpow_le_of_forall_eq_of` (`K = 4(C₁ + 11)` from `|ψ(x, χ)| ≤ C₁ log(N + 2)·x^{1−1/A}`), `exists_prime_eq_of` (`101 + K^A`), `exists_nonsquare_le_of` (`C₀2^A`) and `exists_nonsquare_le_rpow_of` (`C₀(13/δ)^{13}`). See the main README, rounds 482 and 484. All axioms are clean. *(Round 509: `rpow_le_of_forall_eq_of` and `rpow_le_of_forall_eq` hold for every `χ ≠ 1`, since `re_psiChi_ge` assumes nothing about `χ`; at `ε = 1` they give `exists_prime_ne_one`, a prime `p ∤ q` with `χ(p) ≠ 1` and `p ≤ C(log(q + 2))^A` for every Dirichlet character `χ ≠ 1` mod `q` and every `A > 12`. See the main README, round 509.)*

## SquarefreeCount.lean (round 483)

`SquarefreeCount.sum_sqf_eq` is the count `Q(N) = Σ_{d≤N} μ(d)⌊N/d²⌋` of the squarefree `n ≤ N`, from `Σ_{d²∣n} μ(d) = [n squarefree]` (`sum_sq_dvd_moebius`). `SquarefreeCount.abs_sum_sqf_sub_le` is the hyperbola method at `D = ⌊y⌋`: the part `d ≤ D` gives `6N/π²` (`hasSum_moebius_div_sq`, `Σ μ(d)/d² = 1/ζ(2)`) up to `y` and a tail bounded by Abel summation from `|M(t)| ≤ Ct^α` (`abs_sub_sum_le`), and the part `d > D`, rewritten as a sum over `m` of `M(√(N/m)) − M(D)`, is bounded by `Σ_{m≤N/y²}` (`abs_sum_Ioc_le`, `sum_rpow_neg_le`); together `|Q(N) − 6N/π²| ≤ y + CKNy^{α−2}`. With round 472's `MertensExponent.mertens_isBigO_of_zeroFree` (`mertens_le_of_zeroFree`) and `y = N^{1/(3−θ)}`, `SquarefreeCount.squarefree_isBigO_of_zeroFree` gives `Q(x) − 6x/π² = O(x^{1/(3−θ)+η})` from a zero-free half-plane `Re s > θ`; `squarefree_isBigO_twelve_25ths` (`θ = 11/12`) and `squarefree_isBigO_Theta` need no hypothesis. See the main README, round 483. All axioms are clean.

## ExplicitSmooth.lean (round 484)

`ExplicitSmooth.ν₀` is an explicit smoothing: `ν₀ = c₀g` with `g = max(0, (x − 1/2)(2 − x))²` and `c₀ = 1/(2 log 2 − 75/64) ≤ 5`. It is `C¹` (`contDiff_ν₀`, from `hasDerivAt_bump`: at a zero `x` of `h(y) = (y − 1/2)(2 − y)`, `0 ≤ g(y) ≤ h(y)² = o(y − x)`), nonnegative, supported in `[1/2, 2]` and of mass `∫_0^∞ ν₀(x)/x dx = 1` (`mass_ν₀`, from `integral_bump_div`): the properties that `SmoothPerron`, `ChiPNT` and `ChiUniform` ask of a smoothing, for which PNT+'s `SmoothExistence` gives a smooth `ν` with no formula. With `|ν₀| ≤ 2` and `|ν₀′| ≤ 9`, PNT+'s `MellinOfPsi` and round 338's `MediumPNTW.MellinOfPsi_bdd` with their constants (`norm_mellin_le_of_deriv`, `norm_mellin_le_of_norm`) give `|𝓜(Smooth1 ν₀ ε)(s)| ≤ 25/|s|` and `≤ 54/(ε|s|²)`, and `SmoothPerron.mellin_le_geom_of` gives `mellin_ν₀_le_geom`: `|𝓜(Smooth1 ν₀ ε)(σ + it)| ≤ 25^{1−κ}54^κ(σ/2)^{−1−κ}ε^{−κ}(1 + |t|)^{−1−κ}` for `κ ∈ [0, 1]` and `0 < σ ≤ 1`. See the main README, round 484. All axioms are clean.

## QuadIdeals.lean (round 485)

`QuadIdeals` runs rounds 283 and 287's ideal count for `ℚ(ζ₃)` (`Eis.ofNorm_mul`, `Eis.pFactors_cases`, `Eis.card_ofNorm_split`, `Eis.card_ofNorm_inert`, `Eis.card_ofNorm_three`) for every quadratic field. The number `a_K(n)` of ideals of norm `n` is multiplicative in every number field (`card_ofNorm_mul`). In a field of degree `2` every prime splits, is inert or ramifies (`trichotomy`, with the definitions `Split`, `Inert`, `Ramified` through the prime factors of `p𝓞`), and the ideals of norm `p^k` number `k + 1`, `[2 ∣ k]` or `1` (`card_ofNorm_split`, `card_ofNorm_inert`, `card_ofNorm_ramified`). So `a_K = c * 1` for a multiplicative `c` with `c(p) = 1, −1, 0` as `p` splits, is inert or ramifies (`rA_eq`). With a Dirichlet character `χ` equal to `c`, `ζ_K(s) = ζ(s)L(s, χ)` on `Re s > 1` (`dedekindZeta_eq`, with Mathlib's `LSeries_convolution'`), and for `χ ≠ 1`, `L(1, χ)` is the residue of `ζ_K` at `1` in Mathlib's class number formula `tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT` (`LFunction_one_eq_residue`): `2πh_K/(w_K√|D_K|)` for an imaginary quadratic field (`LFunction_one_eq_imag`, with `regulator_eq_one` for unit rank `0`), and `4R_K h_K/(w_K√D_K)` for a real one (`residue_eq_real`). The file imports Mathlib only. See the main README, round 485. ## QuadRing.lean (round 486)

`QuadRing` identifies the ring of integers of a quadratic field. Every number field `K` of degree `2` contains `s` with `s² = d` for a squarefree integer `d ≠ 1` (`exists_sqrt`: complete the square in the minimal polynomial of an element outside `ℚ` and take out the square part with Mathlib's `exists_sq_mul_squarefree`), and every element of `K` is `a + bs` with `a, b ∈ ℚ` (`exists_eq`). For `b ≠ 0` the minimal polynomial of `a + bs` over `ℚ` is `X² − 2aX + (a² − db²)` (`minpoly_eq`), so `a + bs` is an algebraic integer exactly when `2a` and `2b` are integers `A`, `B` with `4 ∣ A² − dB²` (`isIntegral_iff`, with Mathlib's `minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions'` and `int_of_mul_sq`: `dr² ∈ ℤ` forces `r ∈ ℤ` for squarefree `d`). The residues mod `4` (`two_dvd_sub`, `two_dvd_both`, by `decide` in `ZMod 4`) then give the integral bases: `(1, (1 + s)/2)` if `d ≡ 1 (mod 4)` (`span_θ₁`, `basis₁`, `adjoin_θ₁`) and `(1, s)` if `d ≡ 2, 3 (mod 4)` (`span_θ₂`, `basis₂`, `adjoin_θ₂`). If `(1, θ)` is a `ℤ`-basis with `θ² = c + eθ`, Mathlib's `discr K` is `4c + e²` (`discr_eq_of_basis`, from the trace matrix), so `discr K = d` (`discr_θ₁`) or `4d` (`discr_θ₂`), and the minimal polynomials over `ℤ` are `X² − X − (d − 1)/4` (`minpoly_θ₁`) and `X² − d` (`minpoly_θ₂`). The file imports Mathlib only. See the main README, round 486. All axioms are clean.

## QuadSplit.lean (round 487)

`QuadSplit` proves the splitting law of the primes in a quadratic field. For `θ` with `ℤ[θ] = 𝓞 K`, Mathlib's `NumberField.Ideal.primesOverSpanEquivMonicFactorsMod` matches the primes over `p` with the monic irreducible factors of the minimal polynomial of `θ` mod `p`, and the norm of a prime is `p` to the degree of its factor (`absNorm_eq`). With round 485's `QuadIdeals.pFactors_cases`, two distinct linear factors make `p` split, the square of a linear factor makes it ramify, and an irreducible quadratic makes it inert (`split_of_factors`, `ramified_of_factors`, `inert_of_factors`; from the roots of `X² + bX + a`, `split_of_root`, `ramified_of_root`, `inert_of_no_root`). With round 486's generators (`QuadRing.adjoin_θ₁`, `QuadRing.adjoin_θ₂`) and their minimal polynomials `X² − X − (d − 1)/4` and `X² − d`: for `d ≡ 2, 3 (mod 4)`, `p` ramifies if `p ∣ d` or `p = 2` (`ramified_of_dvd₂`, `ramified_two₂`), splits if `p` is odd, `p ∤ d` and `d` is a square mod `p` (`split₂`), and is inert if `d` is not a square mod `p` (`inert₂`); for `d ≡ 1 (mod 4)` the same holds at odd `p` (`ramified_of_dvd₁`, `split₁`, `inert₁`), and `2` splits or is inert as `d ≡ 1` or `5 (mod 8)` (`split_two₁`, `inert_two₁`). The file erases Mathlib's instance "a simple nilpotent additive group is commutative", through which `-x` in `ZMod p` elaborates once `p` is known to be prime and which `ring` does not see through. The file imports Mathlib, `QuadIdeals` and `QuadRing`. See the main README, round 487. All axioms are clean.

## QuadKronecker.lean (round 487)

`QuadKronecker` constructs the Kronecker character of a quadratic field. For `d ≡ 1 (mod 4)` it is `a ↦ J(a | |d|)` on `ZMod |d|` (`jacBot`), whose value at an odd prime `p` is `J(d | p)` by quadratic reciprocity (`jacobiSym_natAbs`) and at `2` is `1` or `−1` as `d ≡ 1` or `5 (mod 8)` (`jacobiSym_two_natAbs`); for `d ≡ 2, 3 (mod 4)` it is `a ↦ J(d | a)` for odd `a` and `0` for even `a`, on `ZMod (4|d|)` (`jacTop`). Its values at the primes are the splitting types of `QuadSplit` (`type_one`, `type_two_three`), so round 485's `QuadIdeals.rA_eq` and `QuadIdeals.dedekindZeta_eq` give `ζ_K = ζ·L(·, χ)` (`dedekindZeta_eq`). A character in such a factorization is not trivial: `ζ_K` has a simple pole at `1`, and `ζ·L(·, 1)` would have a double one (`ne_one_of_eq`, with Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.LFunctionTrivChar_residue_one`). For every number field `K` of degree `2`, `exists_kronecker` gives a quadratic character `χ ≠ 1` modulo `|D_K|` with these properties, and for imaginary `K`, `classNumber_formula` gives `L(1, χ) = 2πh_K/(w_K√|D_K|)` with round 485's `QuadIdeals.LFunction_one_eq_imag`. The file imports Mathlib, `QuadIdeals`, `QuadRing` and `QuadSplit`. See the main README, round 487. All axioms are clean.

`QuadClassNumber` bounds the class numbers of quadratic fields and finds their least inert and split primes. For imaginary `K`, round 487's `QuadKronecker.classNumber_formula` and round 484's explicit bounds for `|L(1, χ)|` give `w_K√|D_K|e^{−2·10²¹}/(2π log log(|D_K| + 16)) ≤ h_K ≤ w_K√|D_K|e^{2·10²¹} log log(|D_K| + 16)/(2π)` (`classNumber_ge`, `classNumber_le`). For real `K`, the residue `4R_K h_K/(w_K√D_K)` of round 485's `QuadIdeals.residue_eq_real` gives the same bounds for `R_K h_K`, with `4` in place of `2π` (`regulator_mul_classNumber_ge`, `regulator_mul_classNumber_le`). With `log log(x + 16) ≤ 40 log log x` for `x ≥ 3` (`loglog_add_le`) and `|D_K| ≥ 3` (Mathlib's `NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two`), `h_K ≥ e^{−2·10²¹}√|D_K|/(80π log log |D_K|)` (`classNumber_ge_loglog`) and `R_K h_K ≥ e^{−2·10²¹}√D_K/(160 log log D_K)` (`regulator_mul_classNumber_ge_loglog`). ## InghamDetect.lean and InghamDensity.lean (round 518)

`InghamDensity.detect_identity`: at a zero `ρ = β + iγ` of `ζ` with `1/2 < β < 1`, for `X ≥ 0` and `Y ≥ 1`, `Σ_n a_n n^{−ρ}(n/Y + ρ − 1)e^{−n/Y} = (1/2π) ∫ G(1/2 − β + iv) dv`, where `a_n = Σ_{d | n, d ≤ X} μ(d)` and `G(w) = M_X(ρ + w)(Z(ρ + w)/w)Γ(w + 1)Y^w` with `Z(s) = (s − 1)ζ(s)` (`PsiOmega.Zr`). On `Re w = 2` the sum is integrated termwise against Mathlib's Mellin inversion of `e^{−x}` (`integral_kernel_line`, the kernel `Γ(w + 1) + (ρ − 1)Γ(w)`); since `Z(ρ) = 0`, `G` is holomorphic on `Re w > −1`, and `SmoothPerron.verticalIntegral_shift` moves the line to `Re(ρ + w) = 1/2`, with `|G(w)|(1 + |Im w|)³` bounded on the strip (`Gfun_strip_bound`, from `HalfPlanePNT.riemannZeta_linear_growth` and `|Γ(x + it)|(1 + |t|)⁵ ≤ KG` on `1/2 ≤ x ≤ 3`). ## LinnikChar.lean and LinnikDeduction.lean (round 520)

`Linnik.linnik_of_charDensity`: let `A ≥ 2`, `B ≥ 0` and `C ≥ 0`, and suppose `CharDensity A B C`: for every modulus `q ≥ 1`, `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1` and `T ≥ 2`, at most `C(qT)^{A(1−σ)}(log qT)^B` Dirichlet characters mod `q` have a zero of `L(·, χ)` in `Re s ≥ σ`, `|Im s| ≤ T`. Then for every `η > 0` there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ K q^{A+η}`. The zero-free region the proof uses beyond `CharDensity` is the pilot's half-plane `Eis.LFunction_ne_zero_of_re_gt` (rounds 492–495). The weight is `e^{−n/x}`, whose Mellin transform `Γ(s)` decays like `e^{−|t|}` on vertical lines (`InghamDensity.norm_Gamma_exp_le`), and `S_χ(x) = Σ_n χ(n)Λ(n)e^{−n/x}` is an integral of `−L′/L(s, χ)Γ(s)x^s` on `Re s = 2` (`perron_exp`, `Sx_eq_integral`). For `χ ≠ 1` the line moves to `Re s = 11/12 + δ` (`integral_pf_shift`) and, below height `T`, across the rectangle `[θ + δ, 11/12 + δ] × [−T, T]` (PNT+'s `HolomorphicOn.vanishesOnRectangle`), when `L(·, χ)` has no zero in `Re s > θ`, `|Im s| < T + 1`; `L′/L` is bounded by `LogDerivDisc.logDeriv_le_ball` (`logDeriv_LFunction_le`), and `norm_Sx_le` gives `|S_χ(x)| ≤ M log(q + 2)(x^{θ+δ} + 2x^{11/12+δ}e^{−T/2})`. `error_le` takes each character at its level, the least `θ_j = min(1/2 + jδ/2, 11/12)` with no zero in `Re s > θ_j`, `|Im s| < T + 1` (`level`, by `Nat.find`), and counts the characters of level `j + 1` by `CharDensity` at `σ = θ_j`. `prime_in_class` adds orthogonality (`totient_mul_SAP`), the trivial character (`re_Sx_one_ge`, with `LeastNonresidue.psi_ge_quarter`) and a class with no prime up to `Y = 10x log x` (`SAP_le_of_noPrime`), at `T = 2 log x + 2`; `total_le` bounds the error terms by `Ktot x^{1−c₀}`, `c₀ = η₀/(48(A + 1))`. `charDensity_twelve` and `linnik_twelve`: the half-plane alone gives `CharDensity 12 0 1`, so Linnik's theorem holds with exponent `12 + η` with no hypothesis. The files import `InghamDetect.lean`, `ChiUniform.lean`, `PNTProgressions.lean` and `LeastNonresidue.lean` here; see the main README, round 520. All axioms are clean.

## LinnikHybrid.lean, LinnikDetect.lean, LinnikDensity.lean and LinnikHalf.lean (round 521)

`LinnikDensity.charDensity_of_LBound`: if `|L(1/2 + it, χ)| ≤ C_L(q(|t| + 2))^c` for every Dirichlet character `χ ≠ 1` modulo every `q ≥ 1` and every real `t`, with `0 < c ≤ 1`, then round 520's `CharDensity (2 + 4c) 10 C` holds with `C = CD(max(C_L, 1), c/(1 + 2c))`, and `linnik_of_critBound` gives Linnik's theorem with exponent `2 + 4c + η`. It is round 518's `densityXi_of_zetaCrit` over the family of characters mod `q`, with one zero per character in place of one per unit window. The mean value over the family (`LinnikHybrid.mean_value_chars`) is orthogonality (`sum_chars_norm_sq_le`) with the mean value theorem in each residue class mod `q`, whose frequencies are `q/(2P)` apart (`row_sum_class`, `mean_value_row`); Gallagher's inequality (`DirMean.gallagher_one`) turns it into large values at one point per character (`large_values_chars`, `large_values_chars_off`). At a zero `ρ` of `L(·, χ)`, `χ ≠ 1`, `LinnikDetect.detect_identityχ` is round 518's identity twisted by `χ`, with `G_χ(w) = M_X(ρ + w, χ)(L(ρ + w, χ)/w)Γ(w + 1)Y^w` and round 520's `Linnik.perron_exp`; since `L(·, χ)` has no pole there are two classes, not three (`dichotomy`). `LinnikDensity.class1_count` counts the polynomial class by dyadic blocks and `large_values_chars_off`; `class2_count` counts the integral class by the bound on the line (`Gχ_left_le`) and the mean value of `M_X(1/2 + it, χ)` at one point per character (`mean_value_mollχ`); `count_nontrivial` takes `X = ⌊Q⌋`, `Y = Q^{1+2c}` and `Q ≥ q(T + 6)`. In `LinnikHalf.lean` (namespace `LinnikDensity`), Mathlib's `LSeries_eq_mul_integral` at the tail `χ(n)1_{n>M}`, continued to `Re s > 0` by `LandauLaplace.eqOn_convex`, gives `L(s, χ) = Σ_{n≤M} χ(n)n^{−s} + s J_M(s)` with `|J_M(s)| ≤ 2(q + 1)M^{−Re s}/Re s` (`LFunction_split`), and at `M = ⌈q(|t| + 2)⌉`, `|L(1/2 + it, χ)| ≤ 11(q(|t| + 2))^{1/2}` (`norm_LFunction_half_le`); hence `CharDensity 4 10 C` and `linnik_four`, Linnik's theorem with exponent `4 + η` and no hypothesis. Besides each other, the files import `DirMean.lean` and `LFunctionGrowth.lean` from `src/`, and `LinnikChar.lean`, `InghamDensity.lean` and `LinnikDeduction.lean` here; see the main README, round 521. All axioms are clean.

The proof is round 517's for `ζ`, made uniform in `q`. `LinnikLindelof.lindelof` is round 470's Lindelöf bound for `L(s, χ)`: `|L(σ + it, χ)|^{±1} ≤ C((q + 2)(|t| + 4))^ε` on `σ ≥ σ₀ > 11/12`, from round 495's half-plane, round 520's `Linnik.logDeriv_LFunction_le` and `ChiUniform.logDeriv_LFunction_right`, with `C` independent of `q` and `χ`. `LinnikFE.norm_LFunction_one_sub_le` is the functional equation on vertical lines for primitive `χ` mod `N`: `|L(1 − σ − it, χ)| ≤ 6N^{σ−1/2}(e⁴|σ + it|)^{σ−1/2}|L(σ + it, χ⁻¹)|` for `1/2 ≤ σ < 1`, from Mathlib's `IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub` with `|ε(χ)| = 1` (`norm_rootNumber`, from `ε(χ)ε(χ⁻¹) = 1` and `ε(χ⁻¹) = conj ε(χ)`). ## LinnikMoment.lean, round 537

`LinnikMoment.refined_moment`: for a complex matrix `A` (rows `ι`, columns `κ`, both finite, `DecidableEq ι`), `b : κ → ℂ` and `μ ≥ 0` with `Re tr(AAᴴ) = card ι · μ`, if `μ·nsq b ≤ nsq (A *ᵥ b)` then `(nsq (A *ᵥ b) − μ·nsq b)²·(nsq (A *ᵥ b) + 2μ·nsq b) ≤ nsq b³·(Re tr((AAᴴ)³) − card ι·μ³)`. `LinnikMoment.refined_moment_cube` is the same with the left side `(nsq (A *ᵥ b) − μ·nsq b)³`. That is Chen–Gupta–Li's Lemma 4.2 (Guth–Maynard's Lemma 4.2 in their citation), `s₁(M) ≤ 2(tr((MM∗)³) − tr(MM∗)³/|W|²)^{1/6} + 2(tr(MM∗)/|W|)^{1/2}`, with constant `1` and squared. `LinnikMoment.refined_moment_chars`: for a finite set `W` of Dirichlet characters mod `q`, a finite set `S` of naturals prime to `q` and `b, c : ℕ → ℂ`, with `N_c = Σ_{n∈S} ‖c n‖²` and `β = Σ_{n∈S} ‖b n‖²`, if `N_c·β ≤ Σ_{χ∈W} ‖Σ_{n∈S} c n·χ n·b n‖²` then `(Σ_{χ∈W} ‖Σ_{n∈S} c n·χ n·b n‖² − N_c·β)³ ≤ β³ · Re Σ_{χ₁,χ₂,χ₃∈W, not all equal} gram χ₁ χ₂·gram χ₂ χ₃·gram χ₃ χ₁`. The proof has no spectral theory: two Cauchy–Schwarz steps give `r³ ≤ ts²` for `r = ‖Aᴴy‖²`, `t = ‖AᴴGy‖²`, `s = ‖y‖²`, `y = Ab`, `G = AAᴴ`. Then `G³ − 3μ²G + 2μ³ = (BA)(BA)ᴴ + 2μ·BBᴴ` with `B = G − μ` (`cube_decomp`, by `module`), and the row-by-row bound (`qf_le_trace`) gives `t − 3μ²r + 2μ³s ≤ (Re tr((AAᴴ)³) − card ι·μ³)·s`. The last step is that `(x − μ)²(x + 2μ)` increases on `[μ, ∞)`. The diagonal of `gram` is `N_c` because `‖χ n‖ = 1` for `n` prime to `q` (Mathlib's `DirichletCharacter.unit_norm_eq_one`), and `sum_triples_split` separates the triples that are all equal. The file imports Mathlib only. See the main README, round 537. All axioms are clean.

*(Round 607: the route's numbers and the certificate's grid are parameters; what follows is the case `SieveRoute.route2333` and `SieveCert.grid2333`, and `linnik_2333` is `SieveMain.linnik_route` there. See the round-607 section below.)* Milestone M8 of `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §13, ~~and the theorem of §0 at `x = q^{2.333}`,~~ *(Round 605: retracted, false when written: `SieveMain.linnik_large` stated `p ≤ 2x` only, without the lower end of §0's theorem; round 605 states `x < p ≤ 2x`; review of round 604, finding 1.)* in seven files. Each file's header states its main theorems, and most headers give the steps of their proofs.

- `SieveChain.chainTU_bound`, `chainTL_bound`: Type II for a chain of primes `rt` and the rough rest of `n`. In the upper window (`W₀ < ∏rt ≤ W₁ ≤ N₁` with `q^{0.401L} ≤ ⌊N₁/W₁⌋` and `⌊N₂/(W₀ + 1)⌋ ≤ q^{0.485L}`) the rest of `n` is the variable. In the lower window (`P₁ < ∏_{i∈S} rt_i ≤ P₂` for a set `S` of indices, `q^{0.401L} ≤ P₁`, `P₂ ≤ q^{0.485L}`) the variable is `∏_S rt`, and the rest of `n` is a tuple of primes. The file imports `SieveProp6.lean`.
- `SieveDecomp`: families of prime tuples cut out by finitely many atoms, with Buchstab's identity (`buchstab_fam`), the cells of a prime (`famI_cells`), splits (`famI_split`) and families that vanish (`famI_vanish`). The file imports `SieveChain.lean`.
- `SieveBuch.Par.decomp`: §6's decomposition to depth 4 as exact identities, each family classified by its cells as `SieveCert` classifies them (evaluated, decomposed, split at `X'`, dropped or vanishing). For `P.Good` *(round 605: added; review of round 604, finding 2)*, weights `g_A ≥ 0` and `g_B`, and leaves within `Err ≥ 0`, `S_{g_A}(z_top) ≥ S_{g_B}(z_top) − D1(g_B) − (1 + n(1 + n(n(n + 2) + 2)))·Err`. The file imports `SieveDecomp.lean`.
- `SieveLeaves.TL_spec`, `TU_spec`, `P6_spec`: the two windows and Proposition 6 on families of atoms. The file imports `SieveBuch.lean`.
- `SieveQ.leaves_ev`: at `x = q^L`, with `z₀ = ⌈q^{a₀}⌉`, `a₀ = L·V/DEN`, `X' = ⌊q^{b₀}⌋`, `b₀ = L(DEN − U2)/DEN`, and `z_top = ⌊√N₂⌋ + 1`: for `η > 0` there are `δ > 0` and `q₀` such that every leaf is within `ηq^L/(φ(q) log q) + q^{L−δ}/φ(q)` for `q ≥ q₀` and `a` a unit mod `q` *(round 606: the unit `a` added; review of round 605, F1)*. `a₀ + b₀ < 0.599L` and `0.515L < b₀ < L − 1` hold because `u₁ > 0.401`, `u₂ < 0.485` and `u₂L > 1`. The file imports `SieveLeaves.lean`.
- `SieveDrop.drop_ev`: for `ε > 0` *(round 605: added; a sibling of review of round 604, finding 2)*, the dropped terms' `B`-count is at most `φ(q)⁻¹(0.88 + ε)x/log x` for large `q`. Each dropped family's count is at most its cells' sum of `Ψ(x/∏rt, rt_last)` (`famI_gB_le`), which `SieveRough.share2_of_cand` and `share4_of_counted4` bound by the cell's cost, and the costs total at most `0.88` (`SieveCert.total_div_le`). The corner cells count only `n = p₁p₂` with both primes in `(z_top/4, z_top]`, `o(x/log x)` (`corner_ev`). The file imports `SieveQ.lean`.
- `SieveMain.linnik_2333`: there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ Kq^{2333/1000}`. For large `q` (`linnik_large`), `S(B, z_top) ≥ φ(q)⁻¹((1 − ε)x/log x − q)` (`TB_ev`, from `SieveRough.theta_near`), and `decomp` with `η = 1/(100·Cdec·L)` and `ε = 1/100` gives `S(A, z_top) ≥ 0.07x/(φ(q) log x) > 0`; a `z_top`-rough `n ∈ (N₁, N₂]` is prime and lies in `(q^L, 2q^L]` *(round 605: it read "at most `2q^L`"; `linnik_large` now states the lower end; review of round 604, finding 1)*. The finitely many smaller `q` take a prime from Mathlib's `Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_modEq`. The file imports `SieveDrop.lean`.

## The route with parameters, and the second goal's phase 1: SieveRoute.lean … Linnik229.lean (round 607)

Round 607 makes the sieve route's numbers parameters and runs the route at `L = 229/100` under one displayed hypothesis, Chen–Gupta–Li's zero-density estimate on `5/7 ≤ σ ≤ 16/21`.

- `SieveRoute`: a route is `L` and a Type II window `[w₁, w₂]` (`Route`), with `RouteOK`: `2 < L ≤ 5/2` and `0 < w₁ < w₂ < 1`. `TypeIIAt` is the conclusion of `SieveTypeII.typeII_step` with `L`, `w₁` and `w₂` in place of `2333/1000`, `401/1000` and `485/1000`. `route2333`, `routeOK2333` and `typeII2333` are round 604's parameters and Type II estimate.
- `SieveCert`: the grid is a parameter (`Grid`: the window's ends `U1`, `U2` and the number `n` of cells a side), with `GridOK`: `H > 0`, `U1 < U2`, `2U2 < DEN`, `2e(n − 1) < DEN`, `4H ≤ V` and `DEN < 2(V + nH)`, each checked by `decide` for a given grid. `grid2333` and `total_le_2333` are round 595's grid and total. `SieveCert229.grid229` is the grid of the window `[4123/10000, 4902/10000]` with `n = 100`, and its total is at most `0.88K` (`total_le_229`, by `decide +kernel`).
- The files from `SieveFamily` to `SieveMain` take a route, a grid or both, with `RouteOK` and `GridOK` where their proofs use them. A route and a grid fit (`SieveQ.Fits`) when `w₁·DEN < U1`, `U2 < w₂·DEN` and `DEN < L·U2`. `SieveMain.linnik_route`: for a route with `RouteOK` and a grid with `GridOK` that fit, given `TypeIIAt` and a total at most `0.88K`, there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ Kq^L`. `linnik_2333` is its case at `route2333` and `grid2333` (`fits2333`).
- The density inputs. `LinnikIngham73.charDensity_ingham73` (D1) gives `7/3 + 4ε` on `1/2 ≤ σ ≤ 5/7` for `0 < ε ≤ 1`; `LinnikCGL.CGLDensity` (D2) is the hypothesis on `5/7 ≤ σ ≤ 16/21`; `LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_hux73` (D3) gives `7/3 + 1/2000` on `16/21 ≤ σ ≤ 5/6`; and `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` gives `101/50` from `5/6` on. Under `CGLDensity` they give the counts of the curve `g73`, which is `1` below `8003/14003`, `(7/3 + 1/2000)(1 − σ)` from there to `5/6`, and `(101/50)(1 − σ)` from `5/6` on (`SieveTypeII73.counts_73`).
- `SieveTypeIIGen.typeII_gen`: Proposition 3′ for a curve whose counts hold and a window whose exponents stay at most `L − 1/25000`. `SieveTypeII73.typeII_73` is its case for `g73` at `L = 229/100` on `[4123/10000, 4902/10000]·L` (`window_73`).
- `Linnik229.linnik_229`: under `CGLDensity`, there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ Kq^{229/100}`. It is `linnik_route` at `route229` and `grid229` (`fits229`), with `typeII229` and `total_le_229`.

## The unconditional exponent `232/100`: LinnikInghamC.lean … Linnik232.lean (round 609)

Round 609 runs the route of round 607 with no hypothesis at `L = 232/100`, from the stack's own density arguments taken as staircases.

- `LinnikInghamC`: round 524's Ingham argument with the detector's `c` as a parameter. `charDensity_ingham_c`: for `0 < ε ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ c ≤ 1`, `δ₀ > 0` and `σ₂ ≤ 11/12` with `(4/3)(1 + 2c)(1/2 − σ₂) + 1 ≤ (2 + 4c)(1 − σ₂)`, there is `C ≥ 0` such that for every `q ≥ 1`, `1/2 + δ₀ ≤ σ ≤ σ₂` and `T ≥ 2`, at most `C(qT)^{(2+4c+4ε)(1−σ)}(log qT)^{10}` characters mod `q` have a zero of `L(·, χ)` in `Re s ≥ σ`, `|Im s| ≤ T`. Round 607's `LinnikIngham73.count_middle73`, its middle range `4/7 ≤ σ ≤ 5/7`, is the case `c = 1/12`, `δ₀ = 1/14`, `σ₂ = 5/7` of `count_middle_c`; `charDensity_ingham73` adds the trivial count below `4/7` and has its own constant *(round 610: it read "`LinnikIngham73` is its case"; review of round 609, F7)*.
- `LinnikStairs`: twenty estimates. `charDensity_in0` … `charDensity_in9` are `charDensity_ingham_c` at `ε = 1/8000` on ten equal steps from `2801/4801` to `3/4`, each with the exponent `3/(2 − σ₂) + 1/2000`, Ingham's curve at the step's right end; `charDensity_hx0` … `charDensity_hx9` are `LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_gen` at the parameters `parHx0` … `parHx9` (`parHx0_good` … `parHx9_good`) on ten equal steps from `3/4` to `5/6`, each with the exponent `3/(3σ₁ − 1) + 1/2000`, Huxley's curve at the step's left end.
- `SieveCurveGlue`: `RangeCounts g lo hi` is `CurveCounts g` restricted to `lo ≤ σ ≤ hi`; a density estimate on a range gives it (`rangeCounts_of_density`), the trivial count gives it for the curve `1` (`rangeCounts_trivial`), two ranges glue across a point into the curve `if σ < mid then g σ else g' σ` (`rangeCounts_glue`), and a range `[1/2, 1]` is `CurveCounts` (`curveCounts_of_range`). `WindowPiece g L m₁ m₂ lo hi` is `WindowOK`'s two inequalities on `lo ≤ β ≤ hi`; pieces glue the same way (`windowPiece_glue`), a piece on `[1/2, 11/12]` is `WindowOK` (`windowOK_of_piece`), and on a range where the curve is affine the two inequalities follow from their values at the corners `β ∈ {lo, hi}`, `m ∈ {m₁, 1, m₂}` and `w ∈ {0, 4·10⁻⁶}` (`windowPiece_affine`; `windowPiece_const` for `A(1 − β)`, `windowPiece_one` for `1`).
- `SieveTypeIIU232`: the curve `gU`, `1` below `2801/4801`, the twenty steps' `A(1 − σ)`, and `(101/50)(1 − σ)` from `5/6` on (`gU_le_one`, `gU_half`); its counts, glued from the trivial count, the twenty steps and `LinnikStep.charDensity_step` (`counts_U`); its window at `L = 232/100` on `[4045/10000, 4825/10000]·L`, twenty-two pieces checked at their corners by `norm_num` (`window_U`); and `SieveTypeIIGen.typeII_gen` there (`typeII_232`).
- `SieveCert232`: `grid232`, the window's grid with `n = 150`, and `gridOK232`. `rows a b` is the sum of the rows `a ≤ i < b` of the total (`rows_eq`); for a grid with `n = 150` the total is the sum of its 25 parts of consecutive rows (`total_eq_rows_of`, `total_eq_rows`), from 2 to 30 rows each, grouped by the kernel's work; each part is at most its bound by `decide +kernel`, one at a time with `Elab.async false` (`rows_0` … `rows_24`), and the bounds sum to at most `0.88K` (`total_le_232`). One kernel check of the whole grid at `n = 150` needed more memory ~~than the machine has~~ *(Round 617: retracted, false when written: than the shell tool's memory cgroup allows, 13.36 GiB in the present container; review of round 616, F1.)*; a part of 15 rows took up to 7.4 GB, so the parts are grouped by their predicted work *(round 610: it read "and so did a part of 15 heavy rows", which was not observed; review of round 609, F2)*.
- `Linnik232.linnik_232`: there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ Kq^{232/100}`. It is `linnik_route` at `route232` and `grid232` (`routeOK232`, `fits232`, `typeII232`, `total_le_232`), with no hypothesis.

## The Weyl-conditional exponent `227/100`: LinnikWeyl.lean … Linnik227.lean (round 612)

Round 612 runs the route of round 607 at `L = 227/100` under two displayed hypotheses: Chen–Gupta–Li's zero-density estimate on `[5/7, 16/21]` (`LinnikCGL.CGLDensity`, round 607) and Petrow–Young's Weyl bound for every character (`LinnikWeyl.PYWeyl`).

- `LinnikWeyl`: `PYWeyl` says that for every `ε > 0` there is `C ≥ 0` such that `‖L(1/2 + it, χ)‖ ≤ C(q(1 + |t|))^{1/6+ε}` for every `q ≥ 1`, every `χ` mod `q` and every real `t`. `class2_empty`: under the bound at one `ε ≤ 1` with constant `CL`, the integral class of round 521's detector is empty once `2·KG·CL·X·(q(T + 2))^{1/6+ε} < δY^{σ−1/2}` (`X ≥ 1`, `Y ≥ 1`, `T ≥ 0`, `1/2 + δ ≤ σ`): `‖I_χ(ρ)‖ < 1/4` for every `χ ≠ 1` with a zero `β + iγ`, `σ ≤ β < 1`, `|γ| ≤ T`. The proof is `LinnikHuxley.class2_count_small`'s integral estimate with the pointwise bound in place of the convexity bound: `‖G_χ‖(1 + |v|)⁵ ≤ A‖M_X‖‖L‖` (`LinnikIngham.Gχ_left_le'`, `A = KG·Y^{1/2−σ}/δ`), `‖M_X‖ ≤ X`, `‖L‖ ≤ CL(q(T + 2))^{1/6+ε}(1 + |v|)²`, and `∫(1 + v²)^{−1} = π`. `class2_finset_empty` and `class2_card_eq_zero` say a finite set of characters detected as in `class2_count_small` is empty.
- `LinnikHuxStepY`: round 607's step (`LinnikHuxStep.charDensity_gen`) with the detector's height `Y = Q^y` as a parameter, `y = (1 + 2cy)/2000` (`ParY`, `Par` with a field `cy`), and the integral class refuted by `class2_empty` in place of the fourth moment: `ParY.Good` is `Par.Good` with `hlam1 : 2y + ε ≤ lam` and `h5 : 1/6 + 2ε + 1/2000 ≤ y(lo − 1/2)` in place of `h3`. `charDensity_genY (Pa) (G : Pa.Good) (hPY : PYWeyl)` gives the exponent `Pa.A` on `[lo, hi]`. At `lo = 5/6` the conditions force `A ≥ 4y + 2ε ≥ 2.00626`, so the exponent `3/(3σ₁ − 1) + 1/2000` is attainable only from ~~`σ₁ ≈ 0.8365`~~ *(Round 613: retracted, false when written: `σ₁ ≈ 0.8362`; `0.8365` is the crossing without the `1/2000`; review of round 612, F3.)* on (`parY_example`, `parY_example'`).
- `LinnikStairs7`: sixty estimates on `[4/7, 11/12]` — twenty Ingham steps, twenty Huxley steps with the fourth moment, twenty with the pointwise bound — each `1/2000` above its curve except the first step above `5/6` (`50159/25000`); above `11/12` the count is at most one (`card_le_one_of_gt`, the zero-free half-plane), which extends the last step to `σ ≤ 1` (`charDensity_hy_top`).
- `SieveTypeIIU227`: the curve `g7` of 62 pieces, its counts under the two hypotheses (`counts_7`; `rangeCounts_cgl` turns `CGLDensity` at `ε = 1/8400` into the counts of `(7/3 + 1/2000)(1 − σ)` on `[5/7, 16/21]`), its window at `L = 227/100` on `[4048/10000, 4858/10000]·L`, 744 corners closed by `norm_num` (`window_7`), and `SieveTypeIIGen.typeII_gen` there (`typeII_227`).
- `SieveCert227`: `grid227`, the window's grid with `n = 100`; `total_le_227` by one `decide +kernel`.
- `Linnik227.linnik_227`: under `CGLDensity` and `PYWeyl`, there is `K` such that for every `q ≥ 1` and every `a` prime to `q` there is a prime `p ≡ a (mod q)` with `p ≤ Kq^{227/100}`.

See the main README, round 612, and `frontier/linnik/SIEVE-ROUTE.md` §17. All axioms are clean.

## The certificate's loss as a parameter: SieveDrop.lean, SieveMain.lean (round 619)

The assembly's threshold `0.88K` was a convention: in `SieveMain.linnik_large` every other loss is a parameter the proof sets to `1/100` of `X = x/log x` (`TB_ev`'s `ε`, `drop_ev`'s `ε`, the leaves' error through `η` and `q ≤ X/100`), and the closing step keeps `7/100` of `X`. Round 619 makes the certificate's loss a parameter too: `SieveDrop.sum_cost_div_of` and `drop_ev_of` take `total/K ≤ c` in the reals, `SieveMain.linnik_large_of` and `linnik_route_of` take `c < 1` and set the losses to shares `ε = (1 − c)/10` of `X` each (`TB_ev`'s, `drop_ev_of`'s, two for the leaves' error and `q ≤ εX`, five in all), which keeps `(1 − c − 5ε)X = (1 − c)X/2`; `SieveDrop.total_div_lt` turns `total < K` into `total/K < 1`, and `SieveMain.linnik_route_lt` is Linnik's theorem with exponent `L` under `total < K`. The `0.88` forms (`sum_cost_div`, `drop_ev`, `linnik_large`, `linnik_route`) are one-line corollaries with their statements unchanged, so `linnik_2333`, `linnik_229`, `linnik_232`, `linnik_227` and `linnik_226` are untouched. The final check prints `linnik_route_lt`'s axioms (443 lines).

The round also sweeps the review of round 618: the headers of `SieveCertDefs.lean`, `SieveCert.lean`, `SieveGrid226.lean` and `SieveCert226.lean` (the import closure of `Mathlib.Data.Nat.Notation` is `Mathlib.Init`'s, 1,339 modules; `total_le_2333` prints no axioms; the moves' two non-verbatim details; a re-wrap), and `build.sh` checks that its module list is in dependency order.
